claims.claim: The current Knesset OData service is v4 at https://knesset.gov.il/OdataV4/ParliamentInfo/.

The older v3 endpoint at https://knesset.gov.il/Odata/ParliamentInfo.svc/ is still up but exposes no vote entity sets: its service document jumps straight from KNS_PlenumSession to KNS_PlmSessionItem, with no KNS_PlenumVote or KNS_PlenumVoteResult.
KNS_PlenumVote is exposed in v4 with fields Id, VoteDateTime, SessionID, ItemID, Ordinal, VoteMethodID, VoteMethodDesc, VoteStatusCode, VoteStatusDesc, VoteTitle, VoteSubject and IsNoConfidenceInGov.

claims.claim: KNS_PlenumVoteResult is exposed in v4 with MkId (not PersonID), VoteID, VoteDate, ResultCode, ResultDesc, LastName, FirstName, SessionID and ItemID.
ResultCode is not a 1=for/2=against/3=abstain mapping: live rows carry ResultCode 7 for 'בעד' and 8 for 'נגד'. Read ResultDesc, not ResultCode.

The v4 service accepts the OData v4 contains(Field,'text') filter syntax (v3 used substringof('text', Field)). The Hebrew literal must be percent-encoded in the request URL; unencoded Hebrew silently returns an empty value array.

KNS_IsraelLawClassificiation is misspelled in the upstream API (double 'i', in both the entity-set name and its ClassificiationID / ClassificiationDesc fields); the correctly-spelled KNS_IsraelLawClassification returns HTTP 404.
The Knesset has 120 seats, unchanged since 1949.
The electoral threshold is 3.25% of valid votes since the March 2014 amendment; was 2% before.
claims.raw_snippet: int list passes the electoral threshold (i.e., the minimum percentage of the vote needed in order to have seats in Knesset, which is 3.25% of the valid votes), the Members of Knesset elected on its behalf form a single joint parliamentary faction, but they may also easily split into several factions, according to the parties that composed the list. It should be noted that running on joint lists is very common in Israeli politics. When is there electoral justification for running on a joint list?

claims.claim: Seat allocation uses the Bader-Ofer method (modified D'Hondt, equivalent to Hagenbach-Bischoff).
PositionID lexicon from KNS_Position: 39 = שר (male Minister), 41 = יו"ר ועדה (Committee Chair), 42 = חבר ועדה (Committee Member), 43 = חבר הכנסת (male MK), 45 = ראש הממשלה (PM).
PositionID 57 = שרה (female Minister) and 61 = חברת הכנסת (female MK).
PositionID 122 = יושב–ראש הכנסת and 123 = יושבת–ראש הכנסת (Knesset Speaker, male/female).
PositionID 54 records faction membership (חבר/ת סיעה, gender-neutral), NOT MK status. Filtering by 54 alone to list MKs is incorrect.

claims.claim: 11 localities in northern and southern Israel had their municipal elections postponed to November 2024 due to wartime evacuation.
claims.raw_snippet: Elections would have been held in 253 localities on the original date; but in 11 of them in northern and southern Israel, whose residents had been evacuated because of the war, the elections were postponed and are now scheduled for November 2024.

claims.claim: KNS_CommitteeSession StatusID 193 resolves in KNS_Status to "מבוטלת" (cancelled) for TypeDesc "ישיבת ועדה". Filter with StatusID ne 193 unless cancelled sessions are wanted. Note the KNS_Status key field is Id, not StatusID.
Knesset number 0 in the Knesset data is the Provisional State Council (מועצת המדינה הזמנית), plenum 15 May 1948 to 14 February 1949.
Hasadna's knesset-data project at github.com/hasadna/knesset-data mirrors Knesset internal databases (including vote tables) to CSV/parquet dumps.

The votes-knesset dataset is published by the Knesset (bard@knesset.gov.il) as a set of CSV resources. The per-file character encoding is NOT documented by the publisher, so the skill tells the agent to detect the encoding rather than asserting Windows-1255 for specific Knesset numbers.
Pre-2014, the Israeli electoral threshold was 2%.
claims.raw_snippet: Until 1992, that threshold was 1% of all votes cast; parties falling under that requirement were not granted seats. The threshold was raised to 1.5% for the 1992 election, and to 2% for the 2003 election. The new Governance Law would raise it to 3.25%, among other measures.

claims.claim: Surplus-vote agreements (heskemei odafim) allow two parties to be treated as one bloc for the leftover-seat allocation round only.

A second round was held on 10 March 2024 in 35 of the 242 localities. The IDI analysis does not state the vote share a mayoral candidate must clear to avoid a runoff, so the skill no longer asserts a percentage.
